messages:
sam: Hey — running into a weird failure when using JSON mode + streaming. The schema validator complains mid-stream and the SDK helper throws.
kai: Ugh, seen that before. Is it a partial chunk problem or malformed JSON at the end?
sam: Looks like partial chunks. Example: model emits first chunk as `{\"items\": [` then a few text chunks, then `]}` but our validator runs on each chunk and rejects because it's not complete JSON.
maria: Are you using the SDK helper that tries to parse every incoming event into a final object? We added a streaming validator recently but maybe it's too eager.
sam: Yup, using the Python SDK helper from devex/examples. Stack trace shows ValueError from json.loads on chunk.
kai: Can you paste a minimal transcript? small clipped version is fine.
sam: Sure — here's a simplified stream:
```
{ "items": [
{ "id": 1, "name": "foo" }
```
then next event
```
, { "id": 2, "name": "bar" }
]
}
```
Validator gets the first two chunks and tries to validate `{ "items": [\n{ "id": 1, "name": "foo" }\n` and crashes.
anya: That makes sense. The streaming helper shouldn't run full-schema validation until stream end. It should do incremental sanity checks only (e.g., ensure tokens are UTF-8 safe), not full JSON parsing.
maria: Agreed. Our previous change to be stricter caused this regression. We wanted to catch bad model outputs early but forgot streaming semantics.
sam: For now I hacked around by buffering until I see matching braces, but that's brittle with nested structures.
kai: Proposed fix: update helper to (1) accumulate chunks into a buffer, (2) try incremental JSON parse only for top-level complete units, (3) expose an option validate_mode: ["none","partial","final"] where default for streaming is "final".
anya: I like expose option. Some users want early partial validation for latency-sensitive apps.
maria: Also need tests: simulate chunked outputs and ensure validator doesn't raise on intermediate chunks. Add e2e test with a mocked streaming socket.
sam: I'll open a small PR with the change. Patch will add a new StreamingJsonValidator class. Quick snippet of intended behavior:
```
validator = StreamingJsonValidator(mode="final")
for chunk in stream:
    validator.feed(chunk)
    if validator.is_complete():
        obj = validator.finalize()
        validate_schema(obj)
```

kai: Nice. For compatibility, ensure existing SDK helper default stays backward-compatible (current strict behavior for non-streaming).
maria: One nuance: some models emit top-level NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON). Validator should detect that and allow per-line validation.
anya: Good call. Add detection: if buffer contains `}\n{` patterns treat as NDJSON and validate per-line.
sam: Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/412 — description + sample stream.
maria: Can you also include the exact error message you saw? Helps triage.
sam: Error was `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 15 (char 14)` from json.loads in helpers/stream.py:52.
kai: Thanks. Assigning to @maria for PR review and @anya for tests.
devex-bot: New PR created by sam: PR #789 - streaming-json-validator (draft)
sam: Pushed a draft. It's minimal, doesn't yet support NDJSON.
maria: I'll take a look tomorrow morning. Quick thought: keep the incremental parse strategy simple to avoid perf hit — use a size threshold before attempting parse.
anya: On tests I'll add a fuzz test that randomly splits valid JSON at random offsets and feed to the validator.
sam: Sweet. Thanks y'all — this was blocking our onboarding sample app which streams a bunch of structured events.
kai: Important to update docs: SDK streaming example should mention validate_mode and NDJSON handling.
maria: Yep, docs + changelog. Also add a note in the migration guide for anyone who relied on the old eager behavior.
sam: Will follow up in the PR with a small sample app diff for onboarding.
anya: :thumbsup: Good ticket, thanks for reporting.
